material.text_fr: La carte postale de Margaux : un phare, et « Il y a du travail ici, si tu veux. »
Marin vous a dit que son père cherche quelqu'un pour l'été, sur son bateau.
Envoyer à Lila les photos du canal, chaque dimanche.
L'avenir du Mistral : le garder, le changer, ou le laisser partir ?
Romy a gardé le dernier néon du Mistral dans sa cave.
Un voisin a vu le camion du brocanteur partir vers le sud avec le tableau.
Lila et Berlin : peut-on vouloir quelqu'un ici, et vouloir son départ pour elle ?
Qui était Odile, et pourquoi est-elle partie ?
Rue de Lancry, au troisième, une fenêtre est encore allumée.

departed.name: Lila Bonnet
departed.why: Lila left for Berlin on 8 January (T8, the platform) and lives there now.

departed.name: Margaux
departed.why: Margaux has gone to Brittany, to Marin's father's, to see the sea.

rules: The whole cast knows the learner: never a stranger's welcome, never the vous of strangers from the group.
The continuation may look for «L.», ask about the rue de Lancry, follow the painting; it never reveals who L. is — that answer belongs to the next authored season.
facts: Le Mistral has closed: its neon went out on the last night. Never stage it as an open café.
Odile's flat is sold to Solvel; the learner kept only Odile's kitchen table.
Margaux has gone to Brittany, to Marin's father's, to see the sea; she writes postcards («Elle est grande.»).
Gus bought the booth's bench and keeps it in his loft.
The painting left with a second-hand dealer's van; it is somewhere in Paris.
Romy's photo essay on the last night is the best thing she has written; M. Marchand sent the learner a Christmas card.
Lila left for Berlin on 8 January; she lives there now. She writes; she is never in a Paris scene.
Odile's last letter has been read: she left two things in Paris, the flat and someone; for the other, «regarde derrière le tableau du Mistral».
Camille Marchand has met the learner and still says vous; the switch to tu belongs to a later season.
The café question of season 1 is closed. Do not reopen it.

draft.logline: After Odile's flat and the café, a postcard from Margaux — 'there is work here, if you want' — pulls you to a small Finistère port where a missing painting, a fisher's offer, and Lila's Sundays of photos make you choose what you will keep and who you will be.
draft.logline_fr: Une carte de Margaux vous mène en Bretagne. Travail, tableau, et photos — que gardez-vous ?
draft.your_arc: You cross to a Finistère fishing town to keep a promise and to follow a clue in the painting; along the way you learn practical work, make uneasy new alliances, and accept friendship at a distance.
draft.first_episode_seed: A wet postcard arrives with a lighthouse on it and Margaux's line: «Il y a du travail ici, si tu veux.» You buy a ticket and call Marin; Romy says she'll come too.

stages.summary: A damp postcard from Margaux with a lighthouse picture arrives and you buy a ticket to Camaret-sur-Mer; Marin and Romy decide to come with you.
At the headland you find Margaux's cottage closed and the locals cautious; the postcard's simple offer feels suddenly large and you must explain who you are.
Maël shows you Margaux's note in the lighthouse log and a small work offer; it is real but ambiguous — the promise is neither a job contract nor a favor, just a place to be useful.
Yann offers you a season's job on his boat to 'see if you last a week' and you accept to prove you can do useful things.
The sea and the rhythm of the boat are harder than you thought; an argument between Yann and Marin about family and pride forces you to choose sides.
You fix a motor under time and weather pressure and earn a nod from Yann; the community counts you as someone who can be trusted with work.
A neighbour mentions a brocante van that left with a framed painting southwards; Augustin and Romy want to track it down and you go with them.
Brigitte the brocante owner is evasive but remembers a buyer and gives a partial address; the trail splits and tempers rise about what should be recovered.
You and Romy find the painting in an old barn; taped behind it is a small fragment of Odile's handwriting — a clue, but not the answer everyone wants.
You remember your commitment to send Lila canal photos on Sundays and start a new thread of postcards and pictures from the port, keeping the ritual alive.
Lila's replies slow and you feel the stretch between Berlin and here; Romy, watching, worries you are making a choice about someone else rather than yourself.
You accept that friendship can survive distance; you make a small public gesture — a printed photo left at the market with a note — and feel steadier.

setting.neighborhood: the small port, the headland and the village streets
setting.tone: quiet, a little windy, practical tenderness — less satire, more close observation
setting.situation: You travel to a Breton port to answer Margaux's postcard, check a fisher's offer, and follow a lead on the missing painting.
setting.situation_fr: Vous allez en Bretagne pour la carte de Margaux et pour chercher le tableau.
setting.why: The material plant p:carte_phare is a postcard from Margaux offering work and an invitation; Margaux is in Brittany (canon) and her line pulls the learner to find what she meant and to keep a promise.

places.description: Small working harbour where fish boats tie up, conversations happen on the quay, and people measure another's seriousness by how they step onto a deck.
places.brief: stone quay with mooring rings, three small fishing boats, stacked lobster pots; cold morning light and wet cobblestones.

places.description: A windswept headland with a white lighthouse that is both object and witness; the postcard image came from here.
places.brief: white tower on black rock, rusted iron rail, gull on a bollard; low overcast light, sea spray on the stones.

places.description: A small wooden trawler with an oil-stained wheel and a tight, serious crew — the place where practical work and family history meet.
places.brief: wooden wheel, coils of rope, diesel smell, patched canvas awning; warm cabin light through porthole at dusk.

places.description: A dusty second‑hand shop near the ramparts where frames pile to the ceiling and the painting might have reappeared.
places.brief: stacked gilt frames, leaning canvases, a brass bell on the counter, grey light through a grimy window.

places.description: A stone cottage Margaux has been staying in; closed like a postcard's back but with a mantel where the card may have been left.
places.brief: stone cottage with blue shutters, a small mantel with postcards, sea-weathered door; warm interior light in the evening.

new_characters.name: Yann Le Guen
new_characters.role: Marin's father; a working fisher who needs a hand for the summer and runs a short, practical household on the boat.
new_characters.personality: quiet, skeptical at first, fiercely practical and proud; he judges by work more than words.
new_characters.wants: Someone who can take a real shift on the boat and whom he can trust at sea.
new_characters.speech_pattern: short sentences, often clipped; uses fishing terms and Breton place-names; speaks to the learner with cautious courtesy.

new_characters.name: Brigitte Lenoir
new_characters.role: Owner of the brocante; she handled the van that took the painting south and remembers faces and small details.
new_characters.personality: gossipy but exacting, warm in the way of someone who sorts objects with care.
new_characters.wants: To catalogue her inventory properly and to be recognised as a small-town businesswoman.
new_characters.speech_pattern: long, descriptive sentences; she names makers and dates and insists on small facts.

new_characters.name: Maël Le Phare
new_characters.role: Caretaker of the headland and lighthouse; he keeps small records of who comes and who goes and left Margaux a note when she moved in.
new_characters.personality: observant, slightly formal, fond of small rituals—tea at four, the logbook at night.
new_characters.wants: To keep the lighthouse as a human place and to pass on its small stories.
new_characters.speech_pattern: measured, almost ceremonial; uses nautical metaphors in everyday speech.

issues: All major moves are plausibly and directly pulled from the listed plants/branches/commitments: Margaux's postcard (p:carte_phare) motivates the trip to Brittany; Marin's father's offer (b:bateau_pere) motivates the boat arc; the brocante van (b:camion_tableau) motivates the painting chase; the weekly photo promise to Lila (c:photos_lila) is preserved. Good alignment.

Be careful not to re-open the café question. Canon says 'Le Mistral has closed' and 'The café question of season 1 is closed. Do not reopen it.' The proposal treats the neon and memory as relics (open thread about the neon) — keep any scenes strictly commemorative, never staging Le Mistral as an operating café.

Respect Lila's canon departure. Lila must remain in Berlin and off-stage; the proposal keeps her as a distant corresponded friend via the photo ritual, which fits the canon rule that she 'is never in a Paris scene.'

Margaux's presence must match canon: she is in Brittany (canon) and currently away; the season must not put her back in Paris or present her as an ongoing café-owner on site. The proposal's portrayal of her cottage as closed fits that constraint.

Tone and learner-facing language: the proposal's new registers (Yann, Maël, Brigitte) are set to 'vous' and to simple speech patterns, which is appropriate for A2-facing French. Ensure actual episode dialogue remains concrete, short sentences and high-frequency vocabulary to meet A2 needs.

Augustin and other Paris characters are listed among the travelling cast. That's allowed, but keep motivations explicit: any character who travels must have a motivating thread from material (Augustin's obsession is grounded in b:camion_tableau). Avoid gratuitous travel that isn't requested by a plant/branch/commitment.
Preserve the rule about the rue de Lancry question: do not reveal who 'L.' is. The proposal keeps the Rue de Lancry thread open; maintain that restriction in any discovered fragments.

Practical detail: the proposal will introduce several new proper nouns and technical vocabulary (fishing terms, brocante cataloguing, lighthouse log). To remain A2-appropriate, introduce and recycle these terms slowly, provide context, and favour actions over abstract exposition.
